title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 2nd Proof The Quran As Decree And Its Miraculousness

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the person carrying the decree?
questions.answer: He is completely truthful and cannot be accused of lying.

questions.question: What is the “decree” in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the Qur’an.

questions.question: From whom does this decree come?
questions.answer: It comes from the Lord and Creator of the universe.

questions.question: What detail shows how widely this decree has been received over time?
questions.answer: In every century, more than three hundred million people have accepted and confirmed it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the special nature of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an is amazing in seven ways and has many signs of being beyond human ability.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do those signs prove about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They prove that it is the speech of the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention another treatise instead of giving a full explanation here?
questions.answer: Because that work already explains the proofs in detail, so this passage moves on briefly.

questions.question: What does the traveller conclude from the Prophet’s role as messenger of the decree?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Prophet would never betray the message by lying.

questions.question: Why would lying be especially impossible for the one delivering this message?
questions.answer: Because lying would go against the message itself and would be disloyal to the One who sent it.

questions.question: What relationship between the messenger and the message strengthens the argument in this passage?
questions.answer: The messenger is presented as faithfully announcing a divine revelation, so his honesty is tied to the truth of what he carries.

questions.question: What central idea does this passage try to prove about the Prophet?
questions.answer: It tries to prove that he is truthful and free from falsehood.

questions.question: What object in his hand is used as evidence for that truthfulness?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, described as a decree.

questions.question: How is the source of that decree presented?
questions.answer: It is presented as coming from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What does the repeated acceptance of the decree in every century suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the message has lasting authority and broad recognition across time.

questions.question: According to the passage, how many broad ways is the Qur’an described as extraordinary?
questions.answer: Seven broad ways.

questions.question: What additional point is made about the Qur’an’s miraculous character?
questions.answer: It is said to have forty aspects that show its miraculous nature.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from those miraculous qualities?
questions.answer: That the Qur’an is the word of the Creator, not a human product.

questions.question: How does the passage use outside scholarship or earlier writing?
questions.answer: It refers readers to another well-known work where these proofs are explained with strong evidence.

questions.question: What moral failure would lying involve for the one who delivers this decree?
questions.answer: It would be both a betrayal of the decree and an act of unfaithfulness toward Allah.

questions.question: What can we infer about the messenger’s duty from this passage?
questions.answer: His duty is to deliver the revelation honestly and exactly as he received it.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the Qur’an compared to in terms of authority?
questions.answer: It is compared to an official command or decree.

questions.question: Why is that comparison important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur’an is not presented as an ordinary book but as a message carrying divine authority.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this decree has a strong historical impact?
questions.answer: It says huge numbers of people in every century have accepted and affirmed it.

questions.question: What does the title given to the Qur’an suggest about its rank?
questions.answer: It suggests greatness, honor, and a very high status.

questions.question: What two major claims are made about the Qur’an’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: That it is wondrous in several ways and that it has many miraculous features.

questions.question: What ultimate truth do those features support?
questions.answer: They support that the Qur’an is from the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why does the speaker not stop to argue all those points in this section?
questions.answer: Because he says another treatise has already covered them in detail with solid proofs.

questions.question: What does the traveller say about the truthfulness of the one who brings this decree?
questions.answer: He says there is no room at all to think that such a person could lie.

questions.question: What two wrongs would falsehood involve in this case?
questions.answer: It would break trust with the divine message and with the One who sent it.

questions.question: What larger lesson about prophethood can be taken from this passage?
questions.answer: A true prophet must be fully trustworthy because he is the carrier of Allah’s revelation.

questions.question: What evidence from revelation is used here to defend the Prophet’s honesty?
questions.answer: The passage uses the Qur’an itself as the main evidence.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an described in relation to people across generations?
questions.answer: It is described as a message accepted by hundreds of millions in each century.

questions.question: What does this repeated acceptance imply about the decree’s influence?
questions.answer: It implies that the message has enduring power and has continued guiding people over time.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s extraordinary qualities?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an shows wonder in seven ways and miraculousness in forty aspects.

questions.question: What belief about the Qur’an follows from those qualities?
questions.answer: That it is the speech of the Creator of everything.

questions.question: How does the passage balance brevity and proof?
questions.answer: It stays brief here but points to another detailed work for fuller evidence.

questions.question: What is the traveller’s final judgment about the messenger of this decree?
questions.answer: He judges that such a messenger cannot possibly be a liar.

questions.question: Why would falsehood be more than a personal sin in this case?
questions.answer: Because it would also be a violation of the message and a betrayal of Allah who sent it.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the greatness of the message with the character of the messenger?
questions.answer: It argues that someone entrusted with such a divine message must be loyal and truthful.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is mainly used in this passage: emotional, historical, or moral-logical?
questions.answer: It mainly uses moral and logical reasoning, while also mentioning historical acceptance.

questions.question: What does the traveller focus on in this section to judge the Prophet’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: He focuses on the divine message the Prophet delivers.

questions.question: What name is given to that divine message?
questions.answer: It is called the Qur’an.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an’s acceptance described?
questions.answer: It is said to be affirmed by more than three hundred million people in every century.

questions.question: Why is this description important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the message has been widely recognized and preserved over long periods.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s remarkable nature?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an is extraordinary in seven ways and miraculous in many further respects.

questions.question: What is one major result of those miraculous qualities?
questions.answer: They point to the Qur’an being from Allah, the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why is another book mentioned in this passage?
questions.answer: It is mentioned as the place where the detailed evidence has already been explained.

questions.question: According to the traveller, why is lying impossible for the Prophet in this role?
questions.answer: Because he is announcing Allah’s decree, and lying would mean betraying both the message and its Sender.

questions.question: What can we infer about trust from this argument?
questions.answer: Trust is essential for a messenger, especially one delivering revelation from Allah.

questions.question: How does this section support belief in the Prophet without discussing miracles from his actions?
questions.answer: It supports belief by pointing to the truth, greatness, and divine source of the revelation he brought.

questions.question: What is the passage’s basic argument in one sentence?
questions.answer: Since the Prophet brought the Qur’an from Allah, he could not be deceitful.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an presented in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a divine command from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What fact is given to show the reach of this command?
questions.answer: Vast numbers of people in every century have accepted and confirmed it.

questions.question: What do the numbers in the passage suggest about the Qur’an’s place in history?
questions.answer: They suggest it has had a continuous and worldwide impact.

questions.question: What two descriptions are given to highlight the Qur’an’s special status?
questions.answer: It is said to be wondrous in seven ways and miraculous in forty aspects.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage connect to these descriptions?
questions.answer: That the Qur’an is truly the word of the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why does the text not explain all forty aspects here?
questions.answer: Because a separate treatise is said to have already explained them carefully with strong proofs.

questions.question: What does the word “conveyor” suggest about the Prophet’s role?
questions.answer: It suggests that he faithfully delivers a message from another source rather than inventing it himself.

questions.question: Why would dishonesty be especially unthinkable in this situation?
questions.answer: Because it would mean breaking the trust of divine revelation and being disloyal to Allah.

questions.question: What view of the Prophet’s character does the traveller reach by the end of the passage?
questions.answer: He sees the Prophet as completely trustworthy in delivering Allah’s message.
